extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 115 psi is about 8 bar, 120 psi about 8.3 bar, 125 psi about 8.6 bar and 150 psi about 10 bar. Temperature: deg C = (deg F - 32) / 1.8, so -10 deg F is about -23 deg C, 0 deg F about -18 deg C, +32 deg F is 0 deg C, +122 deg F is 50 deg C, +125 deg F about 52 deg C, +160 deg F about 71 deg C and +180 deg F about 82 deg C.

A solenoid valve of function 3/2 has 3 ports and 2 positions, 4/2 and 5/2 valves have 4 or 5 ports and 2 positions, and 5/3 valves have 3 positions. A single-solenoid spring-return valve goes back to its normal position when the coil is de-energised; a double-solenoid 2-position valve stays in the last position commanded. A closed-centre 3-position valve blocks all ports in the middle position and an exhaust-centre valve vents the cylinder ports.
extraFacts.source: ISO 1219-1 (fluid power graphical symbols); Indus Hydraulics guide 'Solenoid valve functions explained: 3/2, 5/2 and 5/3 valves'

extraFacts.fact: A solenoid coil is built for one supply type and voltage (for example 24 V DC or 120 V AC); fitting a coil of another voltage or type, or running it from the wrong supply, stops the valve switching or burns out the coil. Pneumatic components must be selected and installed so the system stays safe if the electrical or air supply fails.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414 (pneumatic fluid power, general rules and safety requirements for systems and their components)

extraFacts.fact: NEMA 4 is an enclosure type for indoor or outdoor use that gives protection against windblown dust, rain, splashing water and hose-directed water; it is not an explosion-proof or hazardous-area rating.
extraFacts.source: NEMA 250, Enclosures for Electrical Equipment (1000 Volts Maximum)

extraFacts.fact: Cv is a flow coefficient: the higher the Cv, the more air a valve or manifold passes at a given pressure drop. Valve and manifold Cv should be compared with the Cv the cylinder circuit needs.
extraFacts.source: ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 flow coefficient definition; Indus Hydraulics guide 'Sizing pneumatic valves: Cv, Kv, sonic conductance'

extraFacts.fact: A valve manifold is a common base that carries several valves on one supply and exhaust passage, with each station tapped for the cylinder ports; unused stations are closed with a blanking plate.
extraFacts.source: ARO Ingersoll Rand pneumatic valve manifold catalogue sections; ISO 5599 / ISO 15407 family of valve mounting interfaces

extraFacts.fact: Sibling ARO listings on indushydraulics.com: ARO MaxAir manifolds come in 1/4, 3/8 and 1/2 inch port sizes (2 to 10 stations); ARO Alpha thin manifolds have 1/4 inch ports; ARO E Series manual valves have 1/4 inch ports; ARO K Series valves are 3/8 and 1/2 inch; ARO Sierra 15 body-ported valves have 5/16 inch ports and base-mounted valves 1/8 inch ports; ARO Sierra 18 valves are 18 mm and mount on Sierra manifolds; ARO Sierra high-profile manifolds are listed as SMH51N (2, 4, 6, 8 stations) and SMH81N (2, 4, 8 stations) with 1/8 inch valve ports; ARO MaxAir valves run from 1/4 to 1/2 inch; ARO CAT valves are 1/8 inch (CAT33, CAT44, miniature) or 1/4 inch (high flow).
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics product listings for the ARO ranges named, compiled from the ARO catalogue

faqs.q: What are ARO 200 Series circuitry valves used for?
faqs.a: ARO 200 Series circuitry valves are small 3-way, 2-position, normally closed spool valves operated by a fingertip lever, button, roller, plunger or toggle, used on air cylinders, gates and slides. This listing carries 13 part numbers in 1/8" and 5/32" port sizes with a die-cast zinc inline body.

faqs.q: How do I read an ARO 200 Series part number such as 203-2-C or 224-C?
faqs.a: In the rows on this listing the three digits name the actuator: 201 is a fingertip valve, 202 and 203 are roller levers, 209 a pin plunger, 212 a ball roller, 223 a toggle and 224 a panel button. A -2-C ending is the 5/32" port version (201-2-C, 224-2-C) and a plain -C ending is 1/8" (201-C, 224-C).

faqs.q: Which actuator styles do ARO 200 Series valves come with?
faqs.a: The listing covers fingertip (201-2-C), panel button (224-2-C), roller lever (203-2-C, 202-C), pin plunger (209-2-C), ball roller (212-2-C) and toggle (223-C) actuators. All are spring-return, so the valve goes back to its normal position when you release the operator.

faqs.q: Which port sizes are available on ARO 200 Series circuitry valves?
faqs.a: ARO 200 Series valves on this listing have 5/32" ports (six part numbers ending -2-C, such as 201-2-C) or 1/8" ports (seven part numbers such as 202-C and 212-C). Pick the port to suit your tubing or fitting, and quote the full part number when you order.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature can an ARO 200 Series circuitry valve take?
faqs.a: The listing gives an operating temperature of +32 deg F to +160 deg F, which is 0 deg C to about 71 deg C, and the 1/8" rows (201-C, 209-C, 224-C) are described at 150 psi, about 10 bar. These are not vacuum-operable valves, so use them on positive air pressure only.

faqs.q: What is the ARO 200 Series valve body made from and what media does it handle?
faqs.a: The ARO 200 Series body is die-cast zinc and the valve is a spool type, intended for compressed air on air cylinders, gates and slides. The listing states it is not vacuum operable. For anything other than clean compressed air, send us the medium and we confirm with the maker.

faqs.q: Which documents are available for ARO 200 Series circuitry valves?
faqs.a: This listing holds no datasheet or certificate file for the 200 Series, so ask for the ARO catalogue page or a certificate of conformity in your enquiry and we request it with the order. Quote the exact part number, for example 203-2-C, so the right document is matched.

faqs.q: What fittings and tubing connect to an ARO 200 Series circuitry valve?
faqs.a: A 5/32" or 1/8" ported ARO 200 Series valve takes a matching small-bore fitting and tube, so pick the thread to suit the port. Our [pneumatic fittings and silencers](/c/pneumatic-fittings-silencers) shelf and [pneumatic tubing](/c/pneumatic-tubing) shelf list the matching parts.

faqs.q: How should an ARO 200 Series circuitry valve be mounted and maintained?
faqs.a: Mount the valve rigidly so the actuator, roller or plunger lines up with the cam or limit stop and is not overtravelled. Keep the air supply clean and dry, and replace the valve if the operator sticks or leaks at the exhaust, since these small spool valves are not normally repaired.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ARO 200 Series and ARO 50 Series valves?
faqs.a: ARO 200 Series valves are 3-way, 2-position die-cast zinc valves with 1/8" or 5/32" ports, while the [ARO 50 Series](/p/aro-50-series-pneumatic-valves) is an aluminium side-ported manual valve in both 3-way and 4-way versions with 1/8" ports. Choose 200 Series for a compact limit or signal valve and 50 Series when you need a 4-way.

faqs.q: What are ARO 50 Series pneumatic valves used for?
faqs.a: ARO 50 Series valves are manual 3-way and 4-way, 2-position spool valves with 1/8" NPT ports, operated by lever, button, cam stem or roller. This listing carries 11 part numbers, six 3-way and five 4-way, with an aluminium side-ported body and steel spool.

faqs.q: What do the numbers in ARO 50 Series part numbers like 5030-06 and 5040-01 mean?
faqs.a: In these rows 5030 is the 3-way valve and 5040 the 4-way valve, and the ending sets the actuator: -01 lever with spring return, -02 button, -05 roller cam, -06 cam stem and -10 lever with manual return. So 5040-01 is a 4-way lever valve and 5030-06 a 3-way cam stem valve.

faqs.q: Which ARO 50 Series valve do I need, 3-way or 4-way?
faqs.a: Use a 3-way valve (5030 numbers) to fill and exhaust a single-acting cylinder or signal line, and a 4-way valve (5040 numbers) to drive a double-acting cylinder from both ends. The listing has six 3-way part numbers such as 5030-01 and five 4-way part numbers such as 5040-02.

faqs.q: Which actuators are offered on ARO 50 Series valves?
faqs.a: The rows list lever with spring return (5030-01, 5040-01), button with spring return (5030-02, 5040-02), roller cam (5030-05, 5040-05), cam stem (5030-06, 5040-06), lever with manual return (5030-10, 5040-10) and a manual-return button (5030-12). Choose spring return for momentary action.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature are ARO 50 Series valves rated for?
faqs.a: Several 50 Series rows are described at 150 psi, about 10 bar, and the listing gives -10 deg F to +180 deg F, which is about -23 deg C to 82 deg C. They are not vacuum-operable and are built for lubricated air, so confirm the rating of your exact part number with the maker if you run near the limit.

faqs.q: What materials is the ARO 50 Series valve made from?
faqs.a: The ARO 50 Series has an aluminium body, a steel spool and Buna N (nitrile) seals according to the listing. Nitrile suits compressed air with oil mist, but ask us before using it with synthetic lubricants or aggressive media, and note the listing says lubrication is required.

faqs.q: Which documents come with ARO 50 Series pneumatic valves?

faqs.q: What connects to an ARO 50 Series valve?
faqs.a: ARO 50 Series valves have 1/8" NPT ports, so use 1/8" NPT fittings and tube, or hose, to the cylinder. See our [pneumatic fittings and silencers](/c/pneumatic-fittings-silencers) shelf for thread adapters and our [pneumatic tubing](/c/pneumatic-tubing) for tube.

faqs.q: How do I install and look after an ARO 50 Series valve?
faqs.a: Plumb supply to the inlet and cylinder lines to the working ports, fit the actuator where the operator can reach it, and keep the air lubricated because the listing says lubrication is required. If the valve sticks, check the lubricator is delivering oil rather than forcing the actuator.

faqs.q: How does the ARO 50 Series differ from the ARO E Series manual valves?
faqs.a: The ARO 50 Series is a 1/8" lever, button, cam or roller manual valve, while the [ARO E Series](/p/aro-e-series-pneumatic-valves) is a 1/4" range with foot pedal, treadle and panel-mount versions. Use the 50 Series for a small hand or cam valve and the E Series for a foot-operated valve.

faqs.q: What operating pressure does an ARO Alpha Series valve have?

faqs.q: What are ARO Alpha Series valves made from and do they need lubrication?

faqs.q: What are ARO CAT Series 1/8" port solenoid valves used for?

faqs.q: How do I read ARO part numbers such as CAT33P-012-D and CAT44P-120-A?

faqs.q: Which coil voltages are available on ARO CAT33 and CAT44 valves?
faqs.a: The listing offers 12 V DC (CAT33P-012-D, CAT44P-012-D), 24 V DC (CAT33S-024-L, CAT33P-024-L), 120 V AC (CAT33P-120-A, CAT44P-120-A) and one no-coil valve, CAT33P-000-N.

faqs.q: What is the difference between CAT33 and CAT44 in this ARO range?
faqs.a: Both are 1/8" CAT valves with the same coil options. The CAT44P-012-D row quotes 2 cfm maximum flow and the listing holds no flow figure for the CAT33 rows, so quote the full part number and we confirm the flow with ARO.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature do ARO CAT 1/8" valves have?

faqs.q: What are ARO CAT 1/8" valves made from?

faqs.q: What fittings connect to an ARO CAT 1/8" port valve?

faqs.q: How do I wire and test an ARO CAT33 solenoid valve?

faqs.q: What are ARO E Series pneumatic valves used for?

faqs.q: What do ARO E Series part numbers like E212FS, E252TM and E512LM mean?

The letters set the operator, for example FS is a foot pedal with spring return, TM a treadle with manual return, RS a roller cam and LS a lever.

faqs.q: Which ARO E Series valve do I need for a foot pedal or treadle?
faqs.a: Use E212FS (4-way foot pedal, spring return) or E252FS (3-way foot pedal) for a pedal, and E212TM or E252TM for a treadle with manual return. All have 1/4" ports; pick 4-way to drive a double-acting cylinder.

faqs.q: Which 3-position ARO E Series valves are available?
faqs.a: The listing has two 4-way, 3-position valves, E512LM and E712LS, both lever-operated with 1/4" ports. Use a 3-position valve when you need the cylinder to stop mid-stroke, and check the centre condition with us before ordering.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature are ARO E Series valves rated for?
faqs.a: Row text on this listing gives 150 psi, about 10 bar, and the specification gives -10 deg F to +180 deg F, which is about -23 deg C to 82 deg C. They are not vacuum operable and the listing says lubrication is required.

faqs.q: What is the ARO E Series valve made from?

faqs.q: How should I mount and maintain an ARO E Series manual valve?

faqs.q: What is the difference between ARO E Series and ARO K Series valves?

faqs.q: What are ARO H Series pneumatic valves used for?

faqs.q: What do the ARO H253SS and H254SS part numbers mean?

faqs.q: Which sizes and coil options does the ARO H Series offer?
faqs.a: There are two port sizes, 3/8" (H253SS) and 1/2" (H254SS), each in a 120 V AC coil version and a no-coil version. If you need 12 V or 24 V DC, send us the voltage and we check which coil fits.

faqs.q: Is the ARO H Series a 3-way or 4-way valve?

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature do ARO H Series valves have?

faqs.q: What is the ARO H Series valve made from?

faqs.q: How do I fit a coil to an ARO H254SS-000-N valve?

faqs.q: How do I read ARO K Series part numbers like K214SD-120-A and K513TM?

faqs.q: Which ARO K Series valves are solenoid operated?

faqs.q: Which ARO K Series valves are manual?

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature are ARO K Series valves rated for?

faqs.q: Which MaxAir solenoid sizes and voltages are available?

faqs.q: How much flow does an ARO Sierra 15 valve pass?

faqs.q: What are ARO Sierra 15 body-ported valves used for?
faqs.a: ARO Sierra 15 body-ported valves are compact solenoid valves with 5/16" ports in the body, so they pipe directly without a base. This listing carries four part numbers: S5SSMA-1-G, S5SSMB-1, S5SSMC-1-G and S5SSMD-1.

faqs.q: What do ARO Sierra part numbers like S5SSMD-1 and S5SSMA-1-G mean?
faqs.a: In the rows the letter after M sets the coil: A and C are 120 V AC and B and D are 24 V DC. The -G ending appears on S5SSMA-1-G and S5SSMC-1-G, both 120 V AC valves.

faqs.q: Which coil voltages do ARO Sierra 15 body-ported valves come with?

faqs.q: What flow does an ARO Sierra 15 body-ported valve pass?

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature do these ARO valves handle?

faqs.q: What are ARO Sierra 18 pneumatic valves used for?

faqs.q: Which coil voltages are offered on ARO Sierra 18 valves?
faqs.a: There are four 12 V DC part numbers, five 24 V DC and six 120 V AC. For example M812SD-012-D, M812SD-024-D and M812SD-120-A give the same valve in each voltage.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature do ARO Sierra 18 valves have?
faqs.a: Row text, for example M812SD-120-A, quotes 0 to 115 psi, which is about 8 bar, and the listing gives an ambient range of 0 deg F to +122 deg F, about -18 deg C to 50 deg C. The listing specification says response time is 22 ms.

faqs.q: What are ARO Sierra 18 valves made from?
